**Data Source:** For your final project, you will be working with real RNA-seq count and meta data from breast cancer patients enrolled in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) Breast Invasive Carcinoma (TCGA-BRCA) cohort. This data encompasses diverse subtypes, tumor stages, and patient demographics. Some samples represent tumor tissues; others matched normal control samples from the same patient. TCGA is a landmark cancer genomics program jointly funded by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) and the National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI). TCGA generated comprehensive molecular profiles for over 11,000 patients across 33 cancer types, including bulk RNA-seq DNA methylation, copy number variation, somatic mutations, and clinical annotation. 

This data source includes the following meta data:
•	Patient Demographics
•	Tumor Characteristics
•	Treatment Information
•	Survival Data
•	Sample Details

2)	Gene Selection and Summary Statistics:
  a)	Select One Gene: choose a gene from the dataset that interests you.
  b)	Generate Summary Statistics: Using the count data from the selected gene, compute and report summary statistics, such as mean, median, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum. 
```{r}
# EXPLANATION:
# The raw counts data is in wide form with each sample's counts in columns and 
# genes as rows. The below, first transposes the data frame so that genes become
# columns and samples become rows.

# CITATION (for transposing the raw data): 
# Pivoting. (n.d.). Retrieved September 30, 2026, from https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/articles/pivot.html#longer-then-wider

# Transposes the counts_data so that ensembl id genes become column names with
# their associated values/counts for each sample. Sample names have become row titles.
counts_data_t <- counts_data |> 
  pivot_longer(- ...1, names_to = "barcode", values_to = "value") |>  
  pivot_wider(names_from = ...1, values_from = value)

# EXPLANATION:
# Creates a function that takes in a gene counts data set (where each column is a gene's 
# ensembl ID and each row is a different sample), a specific ensembl ID from the data set,
# a table theme (from ggpubr's table themes), a title for the summary statistics table it
# will generate, and a name for the .png file it will save of the table. The function will
# first generate the following summary statistics for the selected gene: mean, median, 
# minimum, maximum, and standard deviation. Then, the summary will be formatted into a 
# table using the ggpubr package. Ultimately ggsave is used to save the table to a .png 
# file with the file name of your choosing.



# CITATION: 
# https://rpkgs.datanovia.com/ggpubr/reference/ggtexttable.html



summary_stats_table <- function(data_set, ensembl_id, table_theme, table_title, file_name) {
  # Generates the summary statistics for ensembl_id
  stats <- data_set |> summarise(      
    Mean = round(mean(.data[[ensembl_id]]), 2),
    Median = round(median(.data[[ensembl_id]]), 2),
    Min = round(min(.data[[ensembl_id]]), 2),
    Max = round(max(.data[[ensembl_id]]), 2),
    SD = round(sd(.data[[ensembl_id]]), 2)
  ) 
  
  # Creates a table of the summary statistics.
  stats_table <- ggtexttable(
    stats, 
    rows = NULL,
    theme = ttheme(table_theme, base_size = 16)
  ) |> 
    tab_add_title(
      text = table_title,
      face = "bold",
      size = 14,
      just = "center"
    )
  
  # Saves plot as .png for presentation
  ggsave(file_name, plot = stats_table, width = 6, height = 2, dpi = 300)
  
  return(stats_table)
}

# Creates a BRCA1 table of summary statistics by calling the summary_stats_table function
BRCA1_table <- summary_stats_table(
  data_set = counts_data_t,
  ensembl_id = "ENSG00000012048.23",
  table_theme = "mBlue",
  table_title = "BRCA1 Expression Summary Statistics",
  file_name = "BRCA1_stats_table.png"
)

BRCA1_table

# Creates a PALB2 table of summary statistics by calling the summary_stats_table function
PALB2_table <- summary_stats_table(
  data_set = counts_data_t,
  ensembl_id = "ENSG00000083093.10",
  table_theme = "mBlue",
  table_title = "PALB2 Expression Summary Statistics",
  file_name = "PALB2_stats_table.png"
)

PALB2_table

```

```{r}
# EXPLANATION:
# Generates a scatterplot comparing BRCA1 (ENSG00000012048.23) and PALB2 (ENSG00000083093.10)
```

  c)	Create a Violin Plot: Select one covariate from your metadata. Using the count data from the first gene and the selected covariate, generate a violin plot that illustrates the distribution of count data based on the covariate. For example, if you choose “primary_diagnosis”, your plot should display a violin plot for each level in “primary_diagnosis”.
```{r}
# EXPLANATION
# The below, generates a violin plot of BRCA1 gene count across all TCGA-BRCA cohort 
# samples. Counts are grouped by each participant's age at diagnosis as grouped by decade. 
# Ages at diagnosis in the raw meta_data dataset are first replaced by age in years 
# rather than age in days. Next, a new, identical data frame (df) is created that 
# groups ages into ranges by decade (20s, 30s, 40s, etc.). The age categorization is 
# used for creating violin plots for each "decade". 

# In order to create a plot with data from both the counts df and the meta_data df, 
# the two were merged by their shared sample "barcode" column. 

# Ggplot was then used to generate a violin plot with age at diagnosis to generate 
# multiple violin plots on the x-axis and BRCA1 count on the y-axis. Samples that did
# not include age data/were "NA" were filtered out. Each age group's plot has a unique
# color. Boxplots have been added over the violin plots for each age group to cleanly, 
# visually, summarize each group.

# I also ran a quick table function to check that my age categorization worked as I 
# had hoped and for further analysis of the age at diagnosis data.


meta_data_age_cat <- meta_data |> 
  # Adjust age values to be calculated in approximate years rather than days, 
  # rounded to 1 decimal point. Replace the age_at_diagnosis column in the meta_data df.
  mutate(age_at_diagnosis = round(age_at_diagnosis/365, 1)) |> 
  
  # Categorizes participant age at diagnosis for each sample into every 10 year age group
  mutate(age_at_diagnosis = case_when(age_at_diagnosis >= 20 & age_at_diagnosis < 30 ~ "20s",
                   age_at_diagnosis >= 30 & age_at_diagnosis < 40 ~ "30s",
                   age_at_diagnosis >= 40 & age_at_diagnosis < 50 ~ "40s",
                   age_at_diagnosis >= 50 & age_at_diagnosis < 60 ~ "50s",
                   age_at_diagnosis >= 60 & age_at_diagnosis < 70 ~ "60s",
                   age_at_diagnosis >= 70 & age_at_diagnosis < 80 ~ "70s",
                   age_at_diagnosis >= 80 & age_at_diagnosis < 90 ~ "80s",
                   age_at_diagnosis >= 90 ~ "90s+"
                   ))

# Merges the transposed counts and age categorized meta_data data frames by sample barcode
# DFs are in the same wide format with samples as rows and genes/observations as columns
all_BRCA_data <- full_join(x = meta_data_age_cat, y = counts_data_t, by = "barcode")

# Returns groups and their counts within the age at diagnosis column in the categorized meta data df
table(meta_data_age_cat$age_at_diagnosis)

# Violin plot of BRCA1 gene count by age of diagnosis
BRCA1_violin <- ggplot(all_BRCA_data |> filter(!is.na(age_at_diagnosis)), 
                       aes(y = ENSG00000012048.23, 
                           x = age_at_diagnosis, 
                           fill = age_at_diagnosis)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.2, width = 0.2) +
  
  # Adds color and removes the legend as it is redundant with the x-axis label
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel2", guide = "none") + 
  labs(x = "Age at Diagnosis", # Adds axes labels and a title to the violin plot
       y = "BRCA1 Gene Count", 
       title = "BRCA1 Gene Count at Ages of Diagnosis") 

BRCA1_violin

ggsave("BRCA1_violinplot.png", plot = BRCA1_violin) # Saves plot as .png for presentation


```

  d)	Heatmap Analysis: 
    i)	Select 10 genes: Choose a set of 10 different genes from the count matrix for your heatmap.
    ii)	Generate a Heatmap: Use the ComplexHeatmap package in R to create a heatmap of the count data for the selected genes. 
    iii)	Add an Annotation Bar: Include an annotation bar reflecting your chosen covariate for further context and interpretation of the data.
```{r}
# EXPLANATION
# Uses the ComplexHeatmap package to create a heatmap of 10 select genes from the 
# TCGA-BRCA counts data frame. The selected genes were as follows: BRCA1 (ENSG00000012048.23), 
# BRCA2 (ENSG00000139618.16), PALB2 (ENSG00000083093.10), ATM (ENSG00000149311.19), 
# BRIP1 (ENSG00000136492.9),  BARD1 (ENSG00000138376.11), RAD50 (ENSG00000113522.14), 
# RAD51C (ENSG00000108384.15), CHEK2 (ENSG00000183765.23), NBN (ENSG00000104320.14). 
# Counts data associated with the 10 selected genes is pulled from the df by the ensembl 
# IDs which had been previously assigned as row names. Normalized expressions/gene count 
# values are organized into age at diagnosis group (rather than clustered by similarity), 
# making it visually straightforward to compare whether gene expression patterns differ 
# across age decades while still preserving gene-level clustering (on the left) to reveal
# which genes behave similarly.

# Used stack overflow to learn how to save heatmaps to .png files, as ggsave() is a ggplot object
#CITATION: Ann_K. (2022, Feb 4). Re: How to save a heat map created using the ComplexHeatmap 
# package to png format? [Online forum post]. Stack Overflow. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/66044888/how-to-save-a-heat-map-created-using-the-complexheatmap-package-to-png-format.

# Creates new version of counts_data using ensembl IDs under "...1" header as row names
counts_data_gene_rownames <- counts_data |> 
  column_to_rownames(var = "...1")

select_genes <- c("ENSG00000012048.23", "ENSG00000139618.16", "ENSG00000083093.10", 
                  "ENSG00000149311.19", "ENSG00000136492.9", "ENSG00000138376.11", 
                  "ENSG00000113522.14", "ENSG00000108384.15", "ENSG00000183765.23", 
                  "ENSG00000104320.14")

# Subsets rows by name for the 10 selected genes
genes_subset <- counts_data_gene_rownames[select_genes, ] 

# Converts the subset data to a matrix, since Heatmap() requires a matrix datatype for analysis
gene_matrix <- as.matrix(genes_subset) 

# Look up each sample's age group, then drop samples with missing age
age_annotation_data <- meta_data_age_cat$age_at_diagnosis[match(colnames(gene_matrix), 
                                                                meta_data_age_cat$barcode)]

keep <- !is.na(age_annotation_data)
gene_matrix <- gene_matrix[, keep]
age_annotation_data <- age_annotation_data[keep]

# Normalizes each row independently for general comparison between genes using z-scores.
gene_matrix_scaled <- t(scale(t(gene_matrix))) 

# Creates gene labels that are human readable by mapping the ensembl IDs found in the raw 
# data to their associated gene symbols. Ensembl rownames are replaced in the df by 
# readable labels.
gene_symbol_map <- c("ENSG00000012048.23" = "BRCA1", "ENSG00000139618.16" = "BRCA2", 
                     "ENSG00000083093.10" = "PALB2", "ENSG00000149311.19" = "ATM", 
                     "ENSG00000136492.9" = "BRIP1", "ENSG00000138376.11" = "BARD1", 
                     "ENSG00000113522.14" = "RAD50", "ENSG00000108384.15" = "RAD51C", 
                     "ENSG00000183765.23" = "CHEK2", "ENSG00000104320.14" = "NBN") 
rownames(gene_matrix_scaled) <- gene_symbol_map[rownames(gene_matrix_scaled)]

# Creates a Heatmap annotation bar reflecting ages at diagnosis. Each sample is associated 
# with a color in the age bar (including samples with missing age data)


col_annotation <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  AgeGroup = age_annotation_data,
  col = list(AgeGroup = c("20s" = "#BCC69B",
                          "30s" = "#3D3B8E",
                          "40s" = "#6883BA",
                          "50s" = "#B1BEDA",
                          "60s" = "#6EB4D1",
                          "70s" = "#E072A4",
                          "80s" = "#C8AA9E",
                          "90s+" = "#B0E298")
  )
)

# Works with draw() to save Heatmap as .png for presentation.
png("genes_heatmap.png", width = 10, height = 8, units = "in", res = 300)

# Creates a heatmap of 10 selected genes
genes_heatmap_by_age <- Heatmap(gene_matrix_scaled,
  name = "Z-Score",
  # Defines the color gradient for z-scores with smooth interpolation between -2 and 2
  col = colorRamp2(c(-2, 0, 2), c("navy", "white", "firebrick")), 
  top_annotation = col_annotation, # Attaches the annotation bar created above
  show_row_names = TRUE,
  show_column_names = FALSE,
  cluster_columns = FALSE, # Turns off top dendrogram as it is not relevant to current analysis
  cluster_rows = TRUE, # Groups genes with similar expression patterns
  column_title = "Gene Expression by Age at Diagnosis",
  column_order = order(age_annotation_data), # Orders sample z-score data by age group
  row_title = "Genes",
  heatmap_legend_param = list(title = "Z-Score")
  )

genes_heatmap_by_gene <- Heatmap(gene_matrix_scaled,
  name = "Z-Score",
  # Defines the color gradient for z-scores with smooth interpolation between -2 and 2
  col = colorRamp2(c(-2, 0, 2), c("navy", "white", "firebrick")), 
  top_annotation = col_annotation, # Attaches the annotation bar created above
  show_row_names = TRUE,
  show_column_names = FALSE,
  cluster_columns = FALSE, # Turns off top dendrogram as it is not relevant to current analysis
  cluster_rows = TRUE, # Groups genes with similar expression patterns
  column_title = "Gene Expression by Age at Diagnosis",
  #column_order = order(age_annotation_data), # Orders sample z-score data by age group
  row_title = "Genes",
  heatmap_legend_param = list(title = "Z-Score")
  )


draw(genes_heatmap_by_age) 
draw(genes_heatmap_by_gene)
dev.off()

draw(genes_heatmap_by_age)
draw(genes_heatmap_by_gene)

```
```{r}
# EXPLANATION:
# 

table(meta_data$definition)
table(is.na(meta_data$definition))

# --------------------------------------------------------

sample_type_jitter_plot <- function(data_set, ensembl_ID, gene_name, metadata_col) {
  sample_types <- data_set |> 
  filter(!is.na(.data[[metadata_col]])) |> 
  mutate(gene_log = log2(.data[[ensembl_ID]] + 1))

p <- ggplot(sample_types, aes(x = .data[[metadata_col]], y = gene_log, fill = .data[[metadata_col]])) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.4, size = 1) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  stat_compare_means(
    comparisons = list(
      c("Primary solid Tumor", "Solid Tissue Normal"),
      c("Primary solid Tumor", "Metastatic"),
      c("Solid Tissue Normal", "Metastatic")
    ),
    method = "wilcox.test") +
  
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel2", guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Sample Type", 
       y = paste("log2(", gene_name, "Count + 1)"),
       title = str_wrap(paste(gene_name, "Expression by Sample Type"), width = 25))
  
return(p)
}

BRCA1_jitter <- sample_type_jitter_plot(all_BRCA_data, "ENSG00000012048.23", "BRCA1", "definition")
BRCA2_jitter <- sample_type_jitter_plot(all_BRCA_data, "ENSG00000139618.16", "BRCA2", "definition")
PALB2_jitter <- sample_type_jitter_plot(all_BRCA_data, "ENSG00000083093.10", "PALB2", "definition")
```
